name: Zaccur
overview: Zaccur was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically connected to the Merarite clan, descendants of Merari, son of Levi. He is uniquely identified as the son of Jaaziah, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for specific religious duties. His mention appears in the context of the organization of Levitical service.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaccur means 'remembering,' which is a proper name recorded in Scripture but not indicated as given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a characteristic or hope associated with his identity, though no further titles are attributed to him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Zaccur was the son of Jaaziah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 24:27. No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Zaccur's significance lies in his place within the Levitical order, particularly among the Merarites, who had specific roles in the service of the tabernacle. His identification as the son of Jaaziah ties him to the established priestly divisions that facilitated the worship and religious functions of Israel. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his role contributes to the broader understanding of Levitical organization and heritage.
